headline: The Linux Foundation has launched OpenGrid, an open-source effort to give power grid planners common data and tools as data centers push up electricity demand.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 5: a new industry initiative, but early stage with its first product due in 2027.
importance_line: Utilities and regulators planning for data center demand may eventually get shared, open tools, but the first application is not due until 2027 and the project is at an early stage.
source: ET Datacenters, citing the Linux Foundation
summary: ET Datacenters reports, citing the Linux Foundation, that OpenGrid will build open standards, application programming interfaces (software connection points) and a Data Hub of validated data so commercial and open-source grid planning tools can work together, with its first application, the OpenGrid Translator, expected in 2027. It is backed by Breakthrough Energy GRIDS, Global Grid Catalyst, Connected Grid Initiative and Google.org, and cites the International Energy Agency's estimate that more than 2,500 gigawatts of projects are waiting for grid connection.
